rationale: The immediate-isolation execution reproduced the minority leadership a second time (receipt 51408026d38e42f5830a09c290ee3c8b, event 22: became_leader true with reachable_votes 2 against committed_quorum 3, while the flag-off control at event 25 did not win), so the consequence is now observed under two schedules and absent under two settled-schedule runs, with the existing-leader vote guard explaining the difference. That receipt's declared comparisons were nevertheless incomplete, because the harness emits the settled and immediate scenarios with the same result event names, so each comparison saw the other scenario's result event and reported it missing. The successor gives the immediate scenario its own event names (imv_after_restart, imv_partition_election) so every comparison sees exactly one result event; the config-loss claim stays as established and the election consequence is submitted again for a complete comparison. Nothing else is restated.

investigations.hypothesis: A node restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs keeps the snapshot's configuration when committed membership changes sit below the restored commit index, so its quorum arithmetic reflects an obsolete membership and it can win an election its committed configuration would forbid.
investigations.discriminator: Grow a snapshot-age three-voter cluster to five voters, restart the leader, compare the configuration index and server count with the log's latest configuration, then isolate the restarted node with one committed voter and check whether it wins with the smaller quorum while the majority side keeps a leader.

knowledge.statement: A node restarted with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs whose latest snapshot predates committed membership changes resumes with the snapshot's configuration: after growing a three-voter cluster to five voters, the restarted leader held configuration index 1 with three servers while its own log's latest configuration was index 14 with five servers, and the same restart without the flag kept index 14 with five servers.
knowledge.conditions: Config.RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a CommitTrackingLogStore; one snapshot taken before the membership change (automatic snapshots disabled); the committed configuration entry's index at or below the persisted commit index restored by restoreFromCommittedLogs.

gaps.question: Does a leader elected with fewer votes than the committed configuration requires reproduce reliably, under which schedule and partition order, and does the committed configuration's majority side then diverge in committed entries?

interpretations.rationale: The multi-voter configuration loss is established by receipt b15f4b6c55b44402ace926204de9b826 (comparison 0 violated at witness event index 15, control holds at index 18). The minority-election consequence is the part that varied, and the variation now has a sourced explanation. In the settled schedule the partner keeps receiving heartbeats from the majority-side leader, and requestVote refuses a candidate while a leader is known (raft.go:1690-1700), so the isolated node cannot collect its second vote and comparisons 1 and 3 held. With the isolation applied immediately after the restart, so that the partner is also cut off from the majority side, a native run of the same scenario produced the predicted split: leader_below_committed_quorum true with reachable_votes 2 against committed_quorum 3 for the flag-on case, and false for the flag-off control. That mechanism is consistent with the one occurrence of the minority win in receipt 63a30ed680b741199ddd7877237d5874, where the majority side had a leader and the isolated node still won. Source: with the stale three-server configuration quorumSize() (raft.go:1087-1094) returns two and electSelf (raft.go:1999-2060) asks only that list, so one follower's vote suffices, while the committed five-voter configuration needs three; the stale configuration itself comes from restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) advancing lastApplied past the committed configuration before the scan at api.go:604-620, so AddVoter's later entry (api.go:994-1005) is not re-read. The corrected immediate-isolation schedule is submitted again as a successor, because the previous receipt's comparisons were incomplete for a declaration reason (the settled and immediate scenarios shared result event names, so each comparison saw the other scenario's event as missing); its events 22 and 25 nevertheless show the predicted split again: minority leadership with reachable_votes 2 against committed_quorum 3, and no win for the control. No frequency or absence is claimed for either schedule, and no completed comparison is claimed for the election consequence yet.
counterevidence: The flag-off controls keep the committed configuration and cannot win on the isolated side in any execution.

The minority win is schedule dependent: it appeared in two executions (63a30ed680b741199ddd7877237d5874 with the majority side settled, 51408026d38e42f5830a09c290ee3c8b with immediate isolation) and not in two settled-schedule executions, and the difference is explained by whether the isolated partner still hears the majority-side leader.
limitations: The election consequence still awaits a completed comparison; its receipts were incomplete for declaration reasons, not for missing observations.
Only the leadership decision and the coexistence with a majority-side leader are observed; no entry-level divergence is witnessed.
The observation windows are bounded, so no frequency or absence is established.

7da03e78394f41fdad540ae0824ec2a6-gap-1.explanation: Mechanism and schedule dependence now have two controller observations: with immediate isolation the isolated node won with two votes against a committed quorum of three (receipt 51408026d38e42f5830a09c290ee3c8b, event 22; also earlier at 63a30ed680b741199ddd7877237d5874, event 16), while two settled-schedule executions did not produce it because the single committed voter on the isolated side kept hearing the majority-side leader, and requestVote refuses candidates while a leader is known (raft.go:1690-1700). Entry-level divergence between the two leaders is still unwitnessed, so the gap stays open.

interpretations.joint_history: Receipt b15f4b6c55b44402ace926204de9b826 executes the completed multi-voter declaration and supplies this interpretation's own comparisons (configuration loss violated at witness index 15, control holding at index 18). Receipts 51408026d38e42f5830a09c290ee3c8b and 63a30ed680b741199ddd7877237d5874 are further complete executions of the same scenario over the same stores and sizes; they carry the same configuration values (index 1 with three servers against expected index 14 with five; controls at 14 with five) and each additionally records the minority leadership occurrence (events 22 and 16 respectively). None is a fragment of another: every receipt built its own cluster and stores, and only the comparison declarations and event names changed between them.

experiment.revision_reason: Only the comparison declaration and the result event names change: the immediate-isolation scenario now emits imv_after_restart and imv_partition_election, unique to this schedule, so each comparison sees exactly one result event and can complete. The scenario, stores, isolation timing, window and assertions are unchanged from the previous execution.

scope.description: Five-voter cluster whose leading node is restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs after a snapshot that predates the membership change; as soon as NewRaft returns, the restarted node is isolated together with one committed voter while the other three remain connected to each other. Report the rebuilt configuration, whether the restarted node becomes leader, how many votes were reachable, and whether the majority side holds a leader. Run with the flag on and off.
assumptions: The snapshot carries the three-voter bootstrap configuration, so the restarted node's rebuilt configuration is smaller than the committed one.
The isolated side holds two votes; the committed five-voter configuration requires three.
Cutting the partner off from the majority side removes the existing-leader guard that otherwise refuses the vote.
excluded: Any occurrence-rate or absence bound; a bounded observation is not a frequency estimate.
Entry-level divergence after the minority leadership, which needs a separate setup.

experiment.prefix: The harness uses MakeClusterCustom(Peers 3, CommitTrackingLogs, RestoreCommittedLogs), ten Apply calls, an explicit Snapshot(), MakeClusterNoBootstrap(2) merged and two AddVoter calls, ten further Apply calls, then Shutdown and NewRaft on the same logs, stable and snapshots stores with a fresh inmem transport. Immediately after NewRaft it partitions the restarted node plus one committed voter away from the other three and reconnects only that pair, then emits multivoter_after_restart and multivoter_partition_election events carrying the mode, snapshots, restore flag, configuration indices and server counts, the leadership outcome, reachable votes, committed quorum, the majority-side leadership and both terms; no production logic is modified.
experiment.responsibility: The library owns the quorum arithmetic a restarted node applies; with a stale rebuilt configuration it can decide an election that the committed configuration would refuse, which the caller cannot repair through the public API.

comparisons.description: An election on the isolated side must not produce a leader whose support is below the committed configuration's quorum; the defect prediction is that it does.
Control: with the committed configuration rebuilt the isolated side cannot reach three votes and must not produce a leader.
The same run re-checks the rebuilt configuration against the committed log; the defect prediction is the snapshot's configuration.
Control: the identical restart without the flag keeps the committed configuration.
